summary.text: 兴 is the standardized simplified form of 興. The traditional graph is described as people lifting an object together, with its central object uncertain; the modern form is reported as adapted from 興’s cursive form.

formation.text: The formation of traditional 興 is best described as semantic, with a pictorial scene: several hands jointly lift a central object. The received analysis parses it as 舁 plus 同 and explains their combined force, but that account does not settle the original identity of the object or prove the graph’s first design. A competing phonosemantic analysis assigning 型 as phonetic is unsupported by the inspected formation evidence. The entry graph 兴 is a simplified form of 興, reportedly adapted from its cursive form.

history.text: The supplied account describes 兴 as adapted from the cursive form of 興; Unihan identifies 兴 as the simplified variant of 興. The dossier does not establish a detailed dated sequence for this graphic change.
The curated seal-script image is a modern redraw of the received 興 form, not an excavated inscription, and therefore does not establish the appearance or chronology of early forms.

uncertainties.text: The traditional graph is interpreted as people jointly lifting an object, but its exact identity and original spoken name are unresolved. The received 舁-plus-同 account is an old interpretation rather than settled proof of the original structure.

Although one imported account proposes 型 as a phonetic element, the inspected formation sources do not establish that component or role; no component-to-host historical sound relation is supported here.
The evidence reports early inscriptional and manuscript uses but does not establish a complete dated sequence among the character’s meanings.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in oracle-bone and later textual contexts
senses.text: The graph is reported in early contexts with a basic sense of rising or getting up; an oracle-bone use is also described in connection with illness improving. The available evidence does not establish that this was the graph’s original meaning or give a complete chronology.

senses.period: bronze-inscription and manuscript contexts; precise dates unresolved here
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions and manuscript contexts are reported using the character for raising or mobilizing troops. Their relationship in time to the rising sense is not established by this dossier.

Flourishing and prosperity are recorded meanings, including the common modern glosses. The evidence supplied does not establish a specific semantic path from the older rise or mobilization uses to this sense.

limitations.text: The cited sense lists and examples do not establish a dated semantic sequence or prove that any one reported early meaning was the original meaning.

overview.text: 兴 is the simplified form of 興. The traditional graph is interpreted as several people lifting an object together; the object is uncertain. The current character commonly means “flourish” or “prosper.”

relationships.text: 興 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 兴; the supplied account says the simplified graph was adapted from 興’s cursive form.
